title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 360 (Powers and functions of Official Liquidator)

content.overview: The Official Liquidator shall exercise such powers and perform such duties as the Central Government may prescribe. Without prejudice to the generality of that power, the Official Liquidator may exercise all or any of the powers specified in section 290 and such other powers as may be prescribed, and shall perform such duties as the Central Government may prescribe for the purposes of winding up of companies by the Tribunal.
content.glance: Official Liquidator exercises powers and performs duties as prescribed by the Central Government, including powers under s. 290 and other prescribed powers.
content.study: Section 360 defines the functional scope of the Official Liquidator. He exercises such powers and performs such duties as the Central Government may prescribe. Without prejudice to that generality, he may exercise all or any of the powers in section 290 and such other powers as may be prescribed, and shall perform the duties prescribed for Tribunal winding up.

sections.heading: Powers and duties
sections.body: As prescribed by Central Government; may include s. 290 powers and other prescribed powers for Tribunal winding up.

examples.title: Prescribed functions
examples.body: Rules under s. 360 prescribe the manner in which an Official Liquidator is to realise assets and report to the Tribunal in a summary liquidation.

hypotheticals.question: Does the Official Liquidator automatically have all Company Liquidator powers?
